help.tips[0].examples[1].en: We went to Vienna and stayed there for a week.
help.tips[0].check.whyEn: kommen is irregular: the vowel changes to kam and no -te is added, and er has no ending.
help.tips[0].en.text: ich ging, du gingst, er ging, wir gingen, ihr gingt, sie gingen. ich kam / er kam / wir kamen. ich sah / er sah / wir sahen. The plural adds -en; the singular adds nothing.
help.tips[0].en.title: Vowel change, no -te, no ending in ich/er
help.tips[0].en.trap: 'er kamte', 'er gehte' are the commonest errors: adding the regular -te to an irregular verb. If the vowel changed, there is no -te.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: She wrote a letter, drank tea and read until midnight.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: The child fell over, held its knee and then fell asleep straight away.
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: beginnen belongs to the i → a family, like finden/fand and trinken/trank: begann.
help.tips[1].en.text: ei → ie: bleiben/blieb, schreiben/schrieb, steigen/stieg · i → a: finden/fand, trinken/trank, beginnen/begann · e → a: geben/gab, sehen/sah, essen/aß, lesen/las, nehmen/nahm · a → u: fahren/fuhr, tragen/trug, schlagen/schlug · a → ie: schlafen/schlief, fallen/fiel, halten/hielt.
help.tips[1].en.title: The vowel families
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: He stood up, went red and didn't know what to say.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: Then he got up and did what she had said.
help.tips[2].check.whyEn: gehen has its own past stem ging; the wir form adds -en: wir gingen.
help.tips[2].en.text: gehen → ging, stehen → stand, kommen → kam, werden → wurde, sein → war, haben → hatte, tun → tat, wissen → wusste (mixed — next quiz).
help.tips[2].en.title: The unique ones
help.tips[3].check.whyEn: The middle note is the Präteritum: trinken – trank – getrunken, the i → a → u pattern.
help.tips[3].en.text: gehen – ging – gegangen. finden – fand – gefunden. trinken – trank – getrunken. Say the three together; the Präteritum is always the middle note, and the participle usually shows the same family.
help.tips[3].en.title: Learn the triple, sing the middle
help.context.en: It was a grey morning. Anna took her coat, went to the station and travelled into town. There she found a small café, drank a coffee and read the paper. Suddenly she saw an old friend. They stayed the whole afternoon, ate cake and at the end wrote down their new addresses for each other.
help.hookEn: Tell what happened with ging, kam, sah and fuhr: the vowel-changing past forms every story is built on.
help.introEn: Irregular (strong) verbs form the Präteritum by changing the stem vowel and adding no -te: gehen → ging, kommen → kam, sehen → sah, finden → fand, geben → gab, fahren → fuhr, nehmen → nahm, essen → aß, trinken → trank, schreiben → schrieb, lesen → las, schlafen → schlief, bleiben → blieb, werden → wurde. The singular ich/er forms have no ending at all (ich ging, er ging), du takes -st (du gingst), the plural takes -en / -t (wir gingen, ihr gingt, sie gingen). The vowel changes fall into families that help memory — ei → ie (bleiben/blieb, schreiben/schrieb), i → a (finden/fand, trinken/trank, singen/sang), e → a (geben/gab, sehen/sah, essen/aß), a → u (fahren/fuhr, tragen/trug) — and the Präteritum is the middle column of the verb triples you already know from the Perfekt: gehen – ging – gegangen. Around sixty strong verbs cover almost everything you will read in stories and reports; this quiz has the fifteen most frequent.
help.rememberEn[0]: Vowel change + no -te: ging, kam, sah, gab, fuhr.
